newsitem.title: USA: Silicon metal prices to rise next year - Midland.
newsitem.headline: Silicon metal prices to rise next year - Midland.

text.p: Silicon metal prices will rise over the coming year as the supply deficit tightens its grip on the market, said Andrew Lubin, President of Midland Export Ltd.
The market went from a surplus in 1985 to a deficit by last year, when global consumption was 814,000 tonnes with production at 795,000 tonnes, Lubin told an aluminum conference here.
Silicon is used in secondary or recycled aluminum.
"Barring some sort of metals or economic catastrophe, it would be reasonable to expect this supply deficit will continue, and will probably get worse," Lubin said.

About 13 to 19 furnaces of new silicon metal production capacity will be needed if demand forecasts prove accurate, Lubin said, adding that only one new furnace was in the cards at Argentina's Stein company due in 1998.
But Lubin claimed that American silicon producers continue to block imports. "This only exacerbates our domestic supply and price pressures," he added.
Current U.S. silicon metal prices were about 90 to 92 cents per pound, and were expected to reach over $1.00 per pound by the end of next year, Lubin said.
"Most likely we will be looking at closer to a 15 to 20 percent increase once the large quantity of chemical grade silicon is taken out of the supply equation," Lubin said.

Silicon is produced in two grades, chemical and metallurgical. U.S. aluminum alloy producers complained bitterly earlier this year when their margins were squeezed by having to pay more for silicon metal.

Lubin suggested that Brazilian, Chinese and Argentine silicon metal producers, who face dumping duties in the United States, should work together with the aluminum industry to lobby government to end the duties.
The United States needs to import 60,000 tonnes of silicon metal each year, but only China and Brazil have excess capacity to export, Lubin said.

Lubin said the aluminum alloy producers will be competing against each other for silicon metal as suppliers look to switch to chemical grade metal which normally sells at a higher price because it needs more refining.
